title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Issue of an Approved Document
content:
Issue is the moment at which an approved draft of `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` becomes the line's signed evidence of shipment. This page sets out when an approved document may be issued, the freight settlement hold that applies on some types, the issuance fee, and what the issue does to the document's originals.

## Conditions for issue

1. **Cargo on board.** Issue of an approved document follows the loading of its cargo on board. The booking the document covers must show its containers loaded, meaning a booking status of loaded, departed or closed. A booking status of gated in is sufficient only for a document type that carries the received-for-shipment permission. The booking status on the line's records is the evidence.
2. **Prepaid freight hold.** On a type marked below as holding for prepaid freight, a booking whose freight terms are prepaid must show zero charges due on the booking itself (0.00) at the time of issue. The hold is lifted without payment only where the documentation party's credit standing is credit approved and the type also grants the credit exemption. Bookings on collect freight are never held at issue on account of freight.
3. **Service standard.** The line issues within the number of hours shown below, counted from the vessel's departure.

## Effect of issue

4. The issuance fee of the type is charged once for the set being issued.
5. On every type other than the `AHL Sea Waybill`, the issue also puts the type's full set of originals into circulation.
6. The issuance fee can be booked only against a document whose status is issued, and a set of a document is never charged the fee twice. The same status requirement applies to recording the originals put into circulation.

## Tier values

| Document type | Issuance fee (USD per set) | Issue within (hours after departure) | Hold for unpaid prepaid freight | Credit-approved party exempt from the hold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | 45.00 | 24 | No | Yes |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | 35.00 | 4 | No | Yes |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 65.00 | 24 | Yes | Yes |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | 75.00 | 24 | Yes | Yes |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | 95.00 | 48 | Yes | Yes |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | 75.00 | 72 | Yes | No |

## Prepaid hold truth table (types that hold)

| Freight terms | Booking charges due | Party credit approved | Type grants credit exemption | Held at issue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Collect | any | any | any | No |
| Prepaid | 0.00 | any | any | No |
| Prepaid | above 0.00 | Yes | Yes | No |
| Prepaid | above 0.00 | No | any | Yes |
| Prepaid | above 0.00 | Yes | No | Yes |

On the sea waybill and the electronic bill of lading the hold does not exist, so unpaid prepaid freight does not stand in the way of issue.

## Hypothetical example

An `AHL Switch Bill of Lading` is approved; its booking is prepaid, shows 1,200.00 in charges due and belongs to a credit-approved forwarder. The switch type grants no credit exemption, so the document is held until the booking shows zero due. Once issued, it is charged 75.00 for the set.
